A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Inst-IT research, with matching authors, annotation pipeline, dataset and benchmark. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of trained Inst-IT models, benchmark comparisons and training/data-component ablations in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: V2 retains original model evaluations and adds RefCOCOg results, further comparisons, dataset analyses and human annotation-quality ratings.

M1.justification: The SoM-guided GPT-4o annotation pipeline, LLaVA-NeXT architecture, continuous instruction tuning and encoder-freezing recipe remain unchanged. All four annotation/evaluation prompt templates match. V2's dialogue-format explanation and optional SAM2 application discussion do not establish a revised implemented method.

E1.justification: V2 adds RefCOCOg referring-expression evaluation and replaces MM-Vet with ChartQA in the generic image comparison. The eight training-data sources, Inst-IT Bench, ViP-Bench and generic video benchmark coverage remain.

E2.justification: The comparison suite is substantially revised. V2 removes MiniCPM-V2.6 and Qwen2-VL-7B from Inst-IT Bench, MM-1.5 and InternVL2 from retained image comparisons, and IG-VLM, SF-LLaVA, LLaVA-NeXT-Video-DPO, LongVA and MM-1.5-Video-SFT from video comparisons. Conversely, Table 4 adds direct LLaVA-NeXT comparisons on EgoSchema, NExT-QA, VideoMME and TempCompass, where v1 reported no scores for that baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 changes the reported SA-1B selection from splits 1–5 to the first 50% of images in splits 1–10, retaining 51,101 images; this does not establish that training was rerun. V2 also introduces a 500-sample quality study with three independent raters using a 1–5 scale and specifies zero-shot RefCOCOg evaluation. Existing principal model and input-budget settings remain.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantial validation of the dataset through human quality assessment, instance-count distributions, object-category analysis and caption/lexical statistics (Appendix C.2, Figures 9–10, Tables 9–10). It also adds manual failure analysis and an encoder-freezing control for combined image/video data in Table 6. The original component ablation remains, while MMMU results disappear from the training-recipe ablation.

E5.justification: V2 introduces mean±standard-deviation reporting for human quality ratings and inter-rater agreement: 49.8% of samples receive identical ratings and 78.6% have a maximum difference of at most one. V1 has no corresponding reporting. Neither version reports model-performance confidence intervals or repeated-seed estimates.

E6.justification: Retained matched model scores are unchanged, but substantial results are added or removed. V2 newly reports RefCOCOg scores of 63.0 versus 52.2 and ChartQA scores of 68.3 versus 54.8 for Vicuna-7B Inst-IT and its baseline, respectively, alongside new video-baseline, ablation and dataset-quality results. MM-Vet and several comparator results disappear. V2 also introduces inconsistencies: Table 3 labels 87.6 versus 86.4 POPE as +0.2, and Appendix C.2/Table 9 disagree on video-caption length, reporting 323.2 versus 342.2 words.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 retain the same definitions of frame annotation, video summarization and QA generation; notation is refined without changing their mathematics. Neither version contains theoretical guarantees or proofs, and v2's descriptive statistical measures do not introduce new theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same three central contributions: an instance-grounded dataset, an image/video benchmark and continuous instruction tuning that improves instance and generic comprehension. V2's explicit RefCOCOg and ChartQA findings provide additional support and specificity without redefining these central claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds specific failure conditions involving occlusion, blur and small or crowded instances, plus discussion of practical SoM generation and textual instance references in Appendix D. It also interprets the new quality, diversity and lexical analyses. The existing model-scale and GPT-4o-cost limitations are retained after relocation to Appendix E.

D1.justification: V2 explains how annotations become 243k single-turn and multi-turn instruction examples, newly reports eight H100 GPUs and approximately 20/24-hour training times, and explicitly documents benchmark separation from training videos. These expand reproducibility information; the GPT-4o API version, prompt templates, mask-generation tools and project website remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of Ferret, GLaMM and especially Elysium, distinguishing its multi-level image/video annotations from Elysium's simpler video-instance annotations. Table 1 adds structured dataset and benchmark comparisons, and citations are expanded and pruned. The overall positioning around fine-grained instance understanding remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method exposition undergo substantial rewriting and reorganization. Dataset construction now precedes benchmark construction, external instance evaluations receive a separate subsection, and the appendices are reorganized and expanded, with limitations relocated. The title and affiliation text also change.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column format with a redesigned single-column layout and merges v1 Figures 1–2 into Figure 1. It adds comparison/statistics tables and distribution/category graphics, restructures benchmark tables with highlighted gains, and reduces the appendix's twelve-frame annotation example to three frames. The existing video-summary example is moved into a table.

improvement.justification: The new 500-sample human quality audit, RefCOCOg transfer evidence, direct video-baseline comparisons and training documentation strengthen validation and reproducibility. These benefits are tempered by reduced comparison breadth, including removal of MM-Vet where v1's Vicuna Inst-IT scored 38.1 against the baseline's 44.1, and newly introduced numerical inconsistencies. The added validation and documentation nevertheless support a limited net improvement.
